items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: then you have the rumbas of Xavier Cugat, you know and all that, from back in the 30s, 40s and 50s.

ctx.x: I’m going to take a lesson from that. Because sometimes you’re like, oh, how do I nail this cha cha rhythm and tempo especially.

And the rumba, there was a label R – H – U – M – B - A that was confusing for me in my younger days because here I am learning rumba — R – U – M – B – A, the traditional folkloric way, then you have the rumbas of Xavier Cugat, you know and all that, from back in the 30s, 40s and 50s. And I kind of realized it was just a term, a label that they put on the music. And like where I come from it was mostly musica tropical, you know, tropical music. And later on in the 60s the term salsa came into the scene and now…

The rhythms that really got my heart going yesterday were those 6/8 things. And I think it’s such a powerful feeling because you can feel it in two, you can feel it in six, and you can move your body in different ways to it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
